sender.en: “A painting or roofing company” at your door or in your letterbox

name.en: Travelling tradesmen: a big deposit for painting or roof work that never gets done

how.en: A flyer in your letterbox or a visitor at the door offers painting, roofing or other work on your house. They ask for a deposit up front. Some do a little poor work to look real, then disappear with the money. NZ Police say overseas visitors have run this and other rotating scams in Auckland.

text.en: A flyer or a person at your door offers painting or roof work from a company you haven’t heard of.
They push you to book quickly and ask for a large deposit before work starts.
They may do a day or two of poor work, then stop coming and stop answering.
KIWI PRO HOME SERVICES – Exterior painting and roof restoration. Working in your street THIS WEEK ONLY. Special price if you book today. Small deposit secures your spot!

work started and they never came back

en: A company you can’t find any history for, from a flyer or a knock on the door.
“Working in your area”, “this week only” or a special price if you book today.
A large deposit before any work starts.
Little or poor work, then they disappear.
Get quotes from local tradespeople you can check, and don’t decide on the doorstep.
Avoid paying large deposits up front, especially in cash or by bank transfer to a personal account.
If you paid a deposit and the work wasn’t done, report it to Police online or on 105.
Contact your bank about the payment as soon as possible.

sources.title: ‘Think again’: Police send strong message to visitors scamming Kiwis

story.en: In Mt Albert, Auckland, a flyer for a painting company was dropped in a letterbox. The homeowner paid a $27,000 deposit. An associate then sanded the outside of the house poorly over two days and never came back. Police said it was the 14th time in three years that the Auckland City Financial Crime Unit had caught overseas visitors running such scams.
